plan.title: Adipose treated vs control: variance partition + DE
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 adipose bulk RNA-seq samples (6 treated, 6 control), unpaired, single batch, with sex and age recorded per sample and raw Salmon-derived gene counts (12000 genes x 13 columns incl. gene symbol). The question has two parts. First, before testing the treated-vs-control contrast, quantify how much of the per-gene expression variance is explained by condition, sex, and age using variancePartition on voom log-CPM values, with condition and sex as categorical (random-effect) terms and age as a continuous fixed-effect term — this is a design diagnostic, not an inferential test, and it also flags whether age or sex confound the primary contrast enough to worry about power. Second, run the DESeq2 differential expression pipeline: sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap colored by condition/sex), a minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smaller group size), median-of-ratios normalization internal to DESeq2, a design of ~ sex + age_centered + condition with condition releveled so control is the reference, a Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the condition log2FC, and BH-adjusted results at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering. Because age and sex are already in the design as covariates (not regressed out beforehand, per the grounded rule), the treated-vs-control test is adjusted for them, and the variance-partition step from part one becomes the explicit justification for why they are included. Downstream, the DE result feeds a preranked fgsea enrichment on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally) with Reactome and WikiPathways as follow-up collections, and a final report step ties QC, variance shares, DE effect sizes, and enrichment together with full reproducibility bookkeeping. All reference gene sets are human (HGNC symbols), matching the Homo sapiens dataset.

fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark, followed by Reactome and WikiPathways
